claim: pw8 plus a wgmma path for the verify16 (m=128) and verify32 (m=256) loads of the four BF16 layers and the router. At m=128 the math is not hidden under the stream with mma.sync: pooler is 8.6 GFLOP, about 14 µs at mma.sync's ~600 TFLOP/s, on top of a 13 µs stream. pw3's mma.sync TMA path ran 41.7 vs cuBLAS 29.8 in-prepare. wgmma with A from registers removes that: W is decoded from the 12-bit pack straight into the A fragments (no smem round trip), and x arrives as one 128B-swizzled 2D TMA tile per 64-k stage read through a K-major descriptor (N = 128 or 256 tokens). Split-K uses (1, KS, 1) clusters with the pw6 DSMEM reduce, and output goes through a smem transpose as 16-B rows. With the packed stream at about 3.8 TB/s, pooler and unpooler m=128 should reach about 15 judge-µs (cuBLAS 20.3 / 19.3) and qkv about 9.5 (15.4). At m=256: pooler/unpooler about 18-19 (24.5 / 24.1), qkv about 11 (17.4), o about 6 (9.6). Leverage 7.9 (verify16) and 6.6 (verify32) score-µs per µs.
target_shapes: verify16 (m=128): pooler <= 16, unpooler <= 16, qkv_gate <= 11, o <= 6 judge yours (r6: 20.3 / 19.3 / 15.4 / 7.2)
router m=128 / 256: pw-wra (32 CTAs) vs pw8's pw-rtg128 vs the fallback (r6 10.3 / 11.1)
all m <= 32 and router-m<=32 shapes: unchanged from pw8 (identical SASS)
kill_if: Kill the wgmma family if every pw-w* path at m=128 is slower than cuBLAS (torch) in the bake on pooler and unpooler, or if any pw-w* path is INVALID (a layout or descriptor error shows as a one-hot mismatch). Refine instead of kill if m=128 wins but m=256 loses (then x L2 traffic, 32 n-blocks x 4 MB = 128 MB at BN 128, is the limit, and the next step is BN 256 or x multicast across a (2, KS) cluster).

design.kernel: pwg<NWG, NT, ST=4, RTR>. Consumer warpgroups 0..NWG-1 (BN = 64*NWG W rows; warp w of warpgroup i decodes row tile 4i+w = rows 16w..16w+15 of the warpgroup's 64-row block) plus one producer warpgroup (warps 4*NWG..4*NWG+3; one lane issues; with NWG 2 it runs setmaxnreg.dec 40 and the consumers setmaxnreg.inc 232). Stage (1024-aligned, 4 deep) = [x tile NT x 64 k bf16, TMA 2D box {64, NT}, SWIZZLE_128B, rows >= m zero-filled][W chunk RTB x 1536 B, cp.async.bulk], one full barrier with expect_tx = both.
design.pipeline: Per 64-k chunk u: wait full(u) -> 3 x ld.shared.v4 + pw_dec (+ escape XOR) into A[u & 1] -> fence the accumulators -> wgmma.fence -> 4 x wgmma m64nNk16 (descriptor +32 B per k16 step) -> commit -> wgmma.wait_group 1 (chunk u-1 complete) -> pin A[(u-1) & 1] with asm volatile("" : "+r") -> arrive empty(slot of u-1). The decode of chunk u therefore overlaps the MMAs of chunk u-1. At the end: wait_group 0, release the last slot.
design.epilogue: Consumer-only named barrier. D (fragment order = the mma.sync C layout) is staged in the drained ring. Then a cluster barrier. Rank r owns a rectangle of the n-block: RTB/KS whole row tiles when KS <= RTB, otherwise one tile x a 1/(KS/RTB) token range. Its threads issue all KS ld.shared::cluster.v4 loads before the adds, write bf16 (fp32 for the router) into a [tokens][rows] smem transpose buffer, then store 16-B row pieces of out. A final cluster barrier keeps peer smem alive. KS = 1 runs without a cluster.
design.split_k_table: mode a = the largest KS in {1, 2, 4, 8} with NB*KS <= 132; mode b = the next larger one. BN 128 (w2n*): qkv 18x4 = 72 / 18x8 = 144, o 64x2 = 128 / 64x4, pooler 32x4 = 128 / 32x8, unpooler 64x2 = 128 / 64x4. BN 64 (w1n*): qkv 36x2 / 36x4, o 128x1 / 128x2, pooler 64x2 / 64x4, unpooler 128x1 / 128x2. Router (wr, BN 64): 4x8 = 32 CTAs over K' = 16384. KS 7 (from the brief) is not used: rank rectangles must tile the n-block, so KS is limited to divisors of the 8 (or 4) row tiles, or tiles x token ranges.
design.smem_and_registers: w2n128: 384 threads, 113 KB, 168-register entry cap (consumers use at most R135). w1n128: 256 threads, 89 KB, 138 regs. w2n256: 384 threads, 177 KB, setmaxnreg dealloc 40 / alloc 232 (consumer code up to R199, no spill). w1n256: 256 threads, 153 KB, 203 regs. wr: 256 threads, 153 KB, 203 regs. All 0 spill, 0 local loads/stores.
design.m_beyond_256: m > 256 (judge tests 512, 1000) and every odd m are not served by any wgmma path. They run the template fallback (cuBLAS) as before. The kernel itself handles any 1 <= m <= NT through TMA zero fill and masked stores, but only m in {128, 256} are registered.
design.removed: pw3's mma.sync TMA x-ring kernel (pwt) and its paths pw-tm / pw-tms (pw-tmh was already gone), plus the helper only it used. No other kernel was removed: the m<=32 and router paths stay byte-identical to pw8, as requested.
design.stats: New STATS lines in prepare (before the probes and the BAKE table), one per layer and for router hi / lo: distinct exponents, the smallest exponent window covering 99 / 99.9 / 99.99 / 100% of weights, the escape rate of an 8-code exponent window (centred on the mode, and best), the 16-code (current codec) escape rate, the fraction with 1-3 trailing zero mantissa bits, zeros, subnormals, and the Shannon entropy of the 16-bit value / exponent / mantissa. 1.1 s on CPU for all six. On the reference generator's weights: H16 = 10.46 bits/weight (router lo 10.98), Hexp 2.54, Hman 6.97 (incompressible). An 8-code window leaves 1.25-1.36% escapes (router lo 4.0%); the 16-code window of the 12-bit codec leaves 0.01%.

paths: BF16 m=128: pw-w2n128a, pw-w2n128b, pw-w1n128a, pw-w1n128b. BF16 m=256: pw-w2n256a, pw-w2n256b, pw-w1n256a, pw-w1n256b. Router m=128/256: pw-wra (pw-wrb declines: no larger valid KS). Unchanged from pw8: pw-b16t{1,2,4}{g,c}, pw-r2t{2,4}c, pw-b8t1, pw-b8t1c, pw-rtc{1,4}, pw-rtg{16,32}-{1,4}, pw-rtg128. 27 paths.
kernel_count: 25 kernels: 15 pwc (m <= 32 and router, identical to pw8) + 5 pwg (wgmma) + 5 small probe kernels. Local nvcc -cubin of KERNELS_SRC about 6 s (pw8: 4 s). Judge compile has been 32-42 s for pw4-pw6.
compile_check: nvcc 12.8 -arch=sm_90a -cubin -O3 -Xptxas -v: 25/25 kernels 0 spill, 0 stack, no ptxas warnings (no 'wgmma serialized' message). cuobjdump: HGMMA.64x128x16.F32.BF16 / HGMMA.64x256x16.F32.BF16 emitted, 16 per kernel (4 per chunk x prologue, 2 loop copies, tail). WARPGROUP.ARRIVE before each 4-HGMMA batch, WARPGROUP.DEPBAR.LE gsb0, 0x1 only at the wait_group(1) points (not serialized). No LDL/STL in any pwg kernel. USETMAXREG dealloc 0x28 / alloc in the NWG=2 kernels. The first HGMMA of a fresh accumulator was folded to scale-d = 0 (RZ, !UPT). The 20 kernels shared with the current pw8 produce byte-identical SASS. The full CUDA_SRC compiles with -std=c++20 against the minimal torch mock with no errors or warnings.
verification_done_offline: (1) emu_pw9.py (scratchpad) emulates pwg end to end from the natural pack bytes: kernel W addresses, pw_dec, escape walk, A per the PTX register-A layout, B = natural-order x, D per the PTX D layout, fragment staging, rank rectangles summed over KS peers, transpose buffer, 16-B row stores. KS 1, 2, 4 and 8 including KS > RTB (one tile x half the token tiles per rank), odd m (121, 200, 96), and the router K' = 2K with the hi|lo wrap are all bit-exact on one-hot rows and fp64-exact on random rows. Negative control: the r6 permuted-k pack fails on this path (rel. error 1.4), which confirms the packer change is required. (2) A descriptor/swizzle address check: for every token row, k16 step and 16-B half, the descriptor's logical address passed through Swizzle<3,4,3> lands on the TMA SWIZZLE_128B placement. (3) A protocol simulation (sim_pw9.py, 630 randomized schedules, ST 2-4, 1-32 chunks, 4/8 consumer warps): release after wait_group(1) / wait_group(0) never lets the producer refill a slot whose x is still being read by an in-flight wgmma, and never deadlocks. The pw7-style early release is caught 40/40. (4) Lint ok; cpu-check --official 9/9.
risks: Nothing here ran on hardware. The emulator checks the layouts, packing and index math against the PTX ISA's documented layouts; a misread of the hardware (descriptor field, swizzle phase, scale-d semantics) shows up as INVALID in the bake (one-hot mismatch), not as a crash. Descriptor addresses stay inside the CTA's stage, so a wrong field cannot address outside shared memory.

Hang risk: the full/empty protocol and both cluster barriers are simulated. The producer warpgroup exits early; the cluster barriers wait only for non-exited threads (PTX), and the epilogue uses a consumer-only named barrier.

x L2 traffic: BN 128 re-reads x once per n-block: 64 MB at m=128 and 128 MB at m=256 for pooler. If the bake shows m=256 below target while m=128 meets it, that is the cause (next: x multicast across a (2, KS) cluster, or BN 256).
qkv has only 18 n-blocks at BN 128, so mode a gives 72 CTAs and mode b 144 (more than one wave at 1 CTA/SM); expect qkv to be the weakest layer.
Log: STATS (7 lines, about 2.3 KB) prints early, so a long log could push it out of the 16 kB tail. The PW build lines were shortened to '<NG>x<KS>' to keep the total near 12 KB.
One-hot exactness assumes the tensor core keeps bf16 subnormal weights; there are none in these weights (STATS subnormal = 0.0000).
